lora.channel.footer: The channel is which mesh you are on: two radios only hear each other when the name AND the key match. Leave both empty for LongFast, the channel the Meshtastic app ships with. Type a name to join a community mesh, and paste its key if it has one.
lora.channel.key_default: Channel key — leave empty for the default
lora.channel.key_invalid: That is not a channel key. Paste the base64 key from a Meshtastic channel URL (16 or 32 bytes), or leave it empty for the default.
lora.name.footer: The short name is what fits on the node’s own display and in other clients’ lists. Meshtastic allows four BYTES there, so one emoji uses the whole budget.
lora.name.saved: Sent to the node. Other clients pick it up on the next announcement.
lora.name.short.budget: %d of 4 bytes — three or four letters, or one emoji
lora.nodes.empty: Nothing heard yet. A node announces itself every few minutes, so this fills in on its own.
lora.nodes.footer: Every radio this node has heard. Distance is estimated from signal strength unless the radio reports a position.
lora.routing.no_internet.note: Nothing you send touches the relay — not a message, not a read receipt. Anything that cannot go by radio or to a nearby phone waits as pending. Incoming messages still arrive over the internet.
lora.routing.prefer_radio: Prefer my radio over the internet
